recommendation: Stop MuSiQue-fix pilots for now and move to DBEC paper writing. Run a D-BIR-LLM probe only under a strict <=3 day kill-switch if explicitly needed.
core_claim: MuSiQue residual failures are dominated by candidate visibility under long dependency chains, not by DBEC backend admission, scoring, or fixed-pool rank arbitration.
allowed_claims: DBEC's main support-repair mechanism remains supported, especially on 2Wiki and under-selected slices.
MuSiQue residual failures are mostly front-end candidate visibility failures.
Backend admission/scoring/arbitration explains only a small fraction of the missing-gold bucket.
Entity-anchor chain walking has measurable but weak signal in the fixed pool.
Strict title-only anchor matching does not improve the chain-walking probe.
Deterministic dependency-bound lexical expansion does not show an independent advantage over simpler expansion policies.
Strict fixed-pool LLM listwise selection shows nontrivial headroom, but query reformulation and demand-HyDE remain weak and the listwise variant is not yet a practical DBEC method component.
not_allowed_claims: Dependency-bound control is the active component for retrieval expansion.
Admission or scoring is the main MuSiQue bottleneck.
The practical MuSiQue ceiling is a formal theorem rather than a diagnostic estimate.
Fixed-pool candidate generation has been proven exhausted.
Query reformulation or demand-HyDE alone solves the MuSiQue candidate visibility gap.
LLM listwise pool selection improves reader F1 before a reader evaluation is run.
